posts.cooked:
Believe me, I'm the same way.  I grew up with a shrink for a dad, so I know the terminology.  We're not OCD, but we have Obsessive Compulsive Traits (OCTs).  Generally speaking, the difference is both of degree (it isn't crippling) as well as quantity (average people have a few OCTs, people with OCD have lots).  I'm the same way with sleeving as well as things being in a logical order.  Personally, I put all the V5 villains where "Vengeance Five" would be alphabetically (thus currently at the end), and they are sorted alphabetically within that.

My worst OCT by far is with regards to losing things.  I can't STAND to lose things.  It usually triggers a mild to severe panic attack, and I usually have trouble sleeping if I can get past that.  I also sort my closet chromatically.  I'm just weird like that.

posts.name: Silverleaf
posts.cooked:
Yeah, I have a psychology background so it's pretty familiar to me too - I think we all have at least mild OCD-like traits and it's because the stereotypical behaviours like hand washing, checking the security of perimeters (like making sure the modern doors and windows are locked), rituals, etc, would have been important to our survival in our evolutionary past, keeping us safer from infections and attacks and improving group cohesion and such.

That's my excuse. My genes make me do it!

I'm not a sleever because many games don't fit in the original boxes if sleeved, and I don't care about a bit of wear. I am definitely a component bagger though, because things must be segregated. I also prefer to have things in "player bags" if that's feasible, so everything the player needs can be easily handed to them at the beginning of the game, and they can put their own bits away afterwards.

My clothes are ordered by type and then length. Long clothes (dresses with long skirts, longer skirts or shirts with longer sleeves) occupy the left hand side of each type section, with short things on the right. I'll usually avoid similar colours together for ease of identifying individual items.

My games are also organised by size, for efficiency of storage on shelves.

And I'm weird about food too - I have to eat meals consisting of several different foods proportionally. If I have chicken and peas and corn and rice, I can't allow myself to finish the rice before I've started the peas. I can't even eat half the chicken and only a tiny forkful of the other things - I want my meal to be essentially the same meal throughout the eating process, only getting smaller.

I know. It's ridiculous.

posts.name: broccoli
posts.cooked:
My mom and sister are the same way for eating.  In our family, we call them clock eaters, because it's like they make clock-like trips around the plate.  A little of this, a little of that, repeat, with the ultimate goal being to have exactly one bite of everything left at the end of the meal.  As a kid, we used to screw with our mom by pulling a "look over there" and then stealing a bite to make it uneven.  We were mean kids.  Myself and my brother-in-law are what we call food separatists.  We don't like any of our food to touch.  We eat all of A, then all of B, etc, usually saving the best for last.  However, if a portion has a pre-designed separation (like a sandwich cut in half or a fruit cut in fourths), then those portions can be considered individual portions.  My father has to mix all his stuff together into one giant pile.

Human behavior is so fun.
